note: Layers marked used are fetched by the update system and shown with their own source, licence, version and last-updated date. cite-only sources are reference links: no data fetched or bundled.

sources.name: HIFLD Electric Substations and Electric Power Transmission Lines (public-domain US infrastructure data)
sources.licence: Public domain (HIFLD open data release); some line geometry cites OpenStreetMap contributors in its source field
sources.use: Substation and line proximity per US region; compact 345 kV+ overlays
sources.reason: The original HIFLD hosting moved; the dataset is read from ArcGIS Online copies (substations: services.arcgis.com/XG15cJAlne2vxtgt, lines: services1.arcgis.com/Hp6G80Pky0om7QvQ). These are mirrors of unknown update cadence: vintage can be years old and is flagged by refreshDays.

sources.name: PeeringDB API (facilities, IXs)
sources.licence: PeeringDB Acceptable Use Policy (public data; attribution)
sources.use: Facility and exchange counts near each region; unnamed overlay of facilities with 20+ networks
sources.reason: Anonymous API is rate limited (HTTP 429 seen); the fetcher backs off and caches; only derived counts and unnamed points are republished.

sources.name: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 Water Risk Atlas
sources.use: Water stress, drought risk and electricity-sector water risk at state/province or country level
sources.reason: Only the CSV member (18 MB) of the 261 MB zip is read through HTTP range requests; no sub-basin polygon lookup (needs GIS tooling), so values are area-weighted admin-1/country means.

sources.name: Rackmere derived live scores

sources.name: OpenInfraMap (OpenStreetMap power and telecom data)

sources.reason: ODbL share-alike and attribution obligations apply to extracted databases; the public Overpass API returned 'server at capacity' (502) and is not meant for bulk automated use. Cited as the best open worldwide grid map; no extract bundled.

layers.title: Climate normals at region points (NASA POWER)
layers.licence: NASA open data; acknowledge NASA POWER
layers.attribution: Data from the NASA Langley Research Center POWER Project funded through the NASA Earth Science Directorate Applied Science Program
layers.notes: Monthly means at about 0.5 degree resolution; they understate the extreme (99th percentile) design conditions used for cooling design. Not ASHRAE design data.

layers.title: US climate normals 1991-2020 (NOAA)
layers.attribution: Source: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
layers.notes: Station may be up to 80 km from the market centroid. Normals are decadal; refresh interval is long.

layers.title: Interconnection facilities with 20+ networks (global)
layers.licence: PeeringDB Acceptable Use Policy (public data, attribution); only derived counts and unnamed points republished
layers.attribution: Data from PeeringDB (peeringdb.com), used per its Acceptable Use Policy
layers.notes: Unnamed points; network counts self-reported by operators.

layers.title: Network facilities and exchanges near each market
layers.licence: PeeringDB Acceptable Use Policy (public data, attribution); only derived counts and unnamed points republished
layers.attribution: Data from PeeringDB (peeringdb.com), used per its Acceptable Use Policy
layers.notes: Self-reported, user-maintained registry; undercounts private facilities and some regions. Counts are a connectivity proxy, not route diversity.

layers.title: Live indicator scores derived from fetched layers
layers.source: Derived by Rackmere from the layers listed in each region's 'from' map
layers.licence: Derived data; each input layer keeps its own licence and attribution
layers.attribution: Computed from the cited source layers
layers.notes: Recomputed on every refresh. Educational proxies, not site data.

layers.title: US grid carbon intensity (eGRID subregion)
layers.source: U.S. EPA eGRID2023 (subregion output emission rates)
layers.notes: Annual-average location-based rate; hourly and market-based values differ. Subregion found by point-in-polygon on EPA's service.

layers.title: National grid carbon intensity and clean share (Ember)
layers.notes: National averages applied to each market; the market-level grid can differ. Includes US regions' national value for context.

layers.title: FEMA National Risk Index (county)
layers.licence: US Government work (FEMA); data open, cite FEMA
layers.notes: County values, not site values. Scores are relative national percentiles of expected annual loss x social vulnerability / resilience, not probabilities.

layers.title: US seismic design ground motion (USGS)
layers.source: USGS Seismic Design Web Services (ASCE 7-22, 2020 NEHRP-based hazard)
layers.notes: Design-code ground motion at the market centroid; site-specific hazard studies are needed for real sites.

layers.title: Governance indicators (World Bank WGI)
layers.attribution: World Bank, Worldwide Governance Indicators (Kaufmann and Kraay), CC BY 4.0
layers.notes: Country-level perception indicators; not a prediction of project outcomes; says nothing about a city or state.

layers.title: US industrial electricity price by state
layers.source: U.S. EIA, Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.A (Form EIA-861M)
layers.licence: US Government work, public domain (EIA asks for citation)
layers.notes: State-average industrial price for the latest month (preliminary). Not a utility tariff; excludes demand-charge detail.

layers.title: EU industrial electricity price (Eurostat)
layers.source: Eurostat nrg_pc_205 (electricity prices for non-household consumers)
layers.coverage: EU/EEA countries in the region set
layers.notes: National half-yearly averages for a mid-size industrial band; large data centres often pay differently (own contracts). Bi-annual release.

layers.title: Grid proximity (substations and lines near each US market)
layers.source: HIFLD Electric Substations and Transmission Lines
layers.licence: Public domain (US Government HIFLD open data release)
layers.attribution: Source: DHS/CISA HIFLD (mirror hosted on ArcGIS Online)
layers.notes: Proximity of high-voltage facilities is not capacity or headroom. Data vintage is that of the HIFLD release, which can be years old.

layers.title: Transmission lines at 345 kV and above (US, simplified)
layers.source: HIFLD Electric Power Transmission Lines (public-domain US infrastructure data)
layers.licence: Public domain (US Government HIFLD open data release); source field cites OpenStreetMap contributors for some segments
layers.attribution: Source: DHS/CISA HIFLD Electric Power Transmission Lines (mirror hosted on ArcGIS Online); some geometry derived from OpenStreetMap contributors
layers.notes: Simplified to about 1 km; coarse visual overlay, not engineering data.

layers.title: Substations at 345 kV and above (US)
layers.source: HIFLD Electric Substations (public-domain US infrastructure data)
layers.licence: Public domain (US Government HIFLD open data release)
layers.attribution: Source: DHS/CISA HIFLD Electric Substations (mirror hosted on ArcGIS Online)
layers.notes: Positions rounded to 0.01 degree (about 1 km). Voltage as recorded; may be outdated. No headroom/capacity information is public.

layers.title: Water stress (WRI Aqueduct 4.0)
layers.source: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 Water Risk Atlas (baseline annual)
layers.attribution: World Resources Institute, Aqueduct 4.0 (Kuzma et al. 2023), CC BY 4.0
layers.notes: Admin-1 or country area-weighted mean, not the sub-basin at the site: a point-in-basin lookup needs GIS tooling. Local supply and water rights can differ strongly.
